messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector bump yesterday we've got a repro on Qwen2.5 where long-context requests (>=2048) show a perf regression and occasional token drift. Noticing higher p95 and mismatch in KV indexing when we switch to the 'fast_int8_fused' kernel on the fly.

sam: Can you paste the minimal repro and profiler output? I want to see kernel times vs memcpy. :eyes:

alex: Repro is simple-ish. Using dedicated bench run:
```
bench --model qwen2p5 --seq 2048 --batch 4 --profile=nvprof --kernels=selector_latest
```
Profiler top lines:
- forward_attention_fused_int8  34.1ms (per token step)
- kv_cache_update               12.7ms
- memcpy H2D/D2H                6.2ms
- other kernels (softmax/ffn)   9.8ms
Overall p50=120ms -> expected ~90ms.

maria: Interesting. We saw similar when batching heuristic allowed dynamic batch growth mid-sequence. If the kernel swap happens after prefix tokens have been cached with different head layout, the KV index math can be off. Did you see any dim-mismatch logs?

alex: Yes — occasionally: "KV head dim mismatch at update: expected 64 got 32" — but it's noisy, not consistent. Looks like some code path writes half the KV when the fused kernel is used.

dmitry: That sounds like kernel ABI mismatch rather than math. The selector might be choosing an optimized kernel compiled against a different kv-head stride assumption. Which kernel artifacts were deployed? sha: 6a7f3c8 (new) vs previous 3b2e9f1.

lee: Also noticed a tokenizer angle — multilingual inputs from zh/ja tokens produce a different tokenization length distribution which increases chance of batch-growth switching. If earlier prefixes include multi-byte tokens we end up with weird aligned offsets. Repro with zh sample attached.

alex: I attached a short trace (s3://redwood-traces/qwen2p5/kernel-swap/1866543210.trace) — flamegraph shows a spike on the int8 fused kernel at time of swap.

sam: Quick check: can you run the bench with fixed-kernel pin so we can isolate whether the selector is the trigger?
```
bench --model qwen2p5 --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kernel=reference_fp16
bench --model qwen2p5 --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kernel=fast_int8_fused
```
If reference_fp16 matches expected perf and no dim warnings, then selector logic or ABI is suspect.

maria: I ran the pinned tests:
- reference_fp16: p50=92ms, no warnings.
- fast_int8_fused: p50=98ms, intermittent KV warnings and token drift on multilingual sample.
So the kernel alone reproduces the mismatch but selector makes it more frequent due to mid-sequence swaps.

dmitry: That confirms ABI problem in fused kernel. Two likely causes: 1) wrong strides baked into the kernel build for specific head/kv dim configuration, or 2) our wrapper's KV packing path doesn't match the kernel's expected layout when quantizing. Need to diff the build flags for 6a7f3c8 vs 3b2e9f1.

lee: Actionable short-term mitigations:
- Disable dynamic kernel swaps in the selector for Qwen2.5 (force single kernel per-request)
- Tighten batching heuristic: avoid batch growth past initial batch cap for seq>1024
- Add a runtime assertion to check kv stride before calling fused kernel and fallback to safe kernel on mismatch

alex: I opened a small PR that adds the assertion + selector config toggle (PR #3421). Runtime will log and fallback to reference_fp16 if mismatch detected.

runtime-bot: deploy-candidate: runtime/selector v2.7.1-cand deployed to canary pool (tag: canary-186654). Monitoring enabled.

sam: Nice. Can we also add a quick kernel smoke test in CI that builds the fused kernel and runs a KV packing unit test for head sizes [32,64,128]? Prevents regressions.

maria: I'll add the unit test (ticket PERF-842). Also adding a small tokenizer fuzz against zh/ja to ensure token boundaries don't shift initial KV offsets.

dmitry: I'll bisect the kernel changes and check build flags. If we confirm ABI break, we revert the fused kernel blob and schedule a proper rebuild with correct strides.

lee: TL;DR: Immediate: selector toggle + fallback in PR #3421 live on canary. Medium: CI kernel packing tests + tokenizer fuzz. Long: rebuild fused kernel with verified ABI and opt flags.

alex: Thanks — will keep thread updated. If you spot any p99 regressions in canary logs, tag me. :thumbsup:
